B01.name: Vehicle or pedestrian on the runway without clearance
B01.definition: A ground vehicle, tug or person enters an active runway or its protected area without an ATC clearance.

B02.name: Landing on a taxiway or the wrong runway at night
B02.definition: At night or in low light the crew lines up on and lands, or nearly lands, on a taxiway or a runway other than the one assigned.

B03.name: Veer-off during landing in a strong or gusty crosswind
B03.definition: In a strong or gusty crosswind the aircraft drifts and veers off the side of the runway during the landing roll.

B04.name: Overrun on a contaminated runway
B04.definition: On a wet, slushy, snowy or icy runway braking is poor and the aircraft overruns the end of the runway.

B05.name: Stall warning or upset during a go-around
B05.definition: During a go-around or missed approach the aircraft pitches up with high thrust, energy is mismanaged, and a stall warning or upset follows.

B06.name: Wake turbulence upset on approach
B06.definition: Wake vortices from a preceding heavier aircraft cause a sudden roll or pitch upset on approach or departure.

B07.name: Loss of separation caused by an ATC clearance
B07.definition: A controller clearance or instruction puts two aircraft into conflict, leading to loss of separation or a TCAS alert.

B08.name: TCAS resolution advisory after a level bust
B08.definition: The aircraft climbs or descends through its cleared altitude (level bust) and a TCAS resolution advisory follows.

B09.name: Hydraulic system failure in flight
B09.definition: Loss of fluid or pressure in a hydraulic system in flight degrades flight controls, brakes or landing gear.

B10.name: Landing gear did not extend
B10.definition: One or more landing gear legs fail to extend or lock down, requiring alternate extension or a gear-up landing.

B11.name: Terrain warning on a non-precision approach
B11.definition: During a non-precision or visual approach the aircraft descends too low and the terrain awareness system warns of terrain or obstacles.

B12.name: GNSS interference or spoofing
B12.definition: Satellite navigation signals are jammed or spoofed, giving false position, lost RNP capability or incorrect time, often near conflict zones.

B13.name: Engine shutdown after loss of oil pressure
B13.definition: Low oil pressure or oil loss in flight leads the crew to shut an engine down as a precaution.

B14.name: Takeoff with frost or ice not removed
B14.definition: The aircraft departs or begins to depart with frost, snow or ice on its wings because it was not removed or the fluid failed.

B15.name: Bird ingestion damaging an engine on takeoff or climb
B15.definition: One or more birds are ingested into an engine during takeoff or initial climb, causing vibration, surging or loss of thrust.

B16.name: Bird strike damaging the windshield or nose on approach
B16.definition: A large bird or flock strikes the windshield, radome or nose on approach or descent and causes visible damage.

B17.name: Lithium battery fire from a passenger device
B17.definition: A phone, laptop, power bank or other lithium battery device overheats, smokes or catches fire in the cabin.

B18.name: Electrical smoke or burning smell in the flight deck
B18.definition: Smoke, fumes or a burning electrical smell appears in the flight deck, often traced to wiring, a display or a window heater.

B19.name: Low fuel after holding or a diversion
B19.definition: Extended holding, a missed approach or a diversion leaves the aircraft close to or below final reserve fuel, and the crew declares minimum fuel or a fuel emergency.

B20.name: Pushback or towing collision
B20.definition: During pushback or towing the tug, towbar or aircraft strikes another aircraft, a vehicle or a fixed object.

B21.name: Disruptive or unruly passenger
B21.definition: A passenger is aggressive, intoxicated or refuses crew instructions, interfering with the crew or other passengers.

B22.name: Tail strike on takeoff
B22.definition: The tail strikes the runway during takeoff rotation, often after early or fast rotation or a wrong takeoff speed or weight.

B23.name: Windshear on final approach
B23.definition: A sudden change in wind speed or direction on approach, often near a thunderstorm or microburst, causes loss of airspeed and a windshear warning.

B24.name: Landing short of the runway
B24.definition: The aircraft touches down before the runway threshold, on the approach lights or in the undershoot area.

B25.name: Airframe icing in flight
B25.definition: Ice builds on the wings, tail or windshield in flight in icing conditions, degrading performance or handling.

B26.name: Unreliable airspeed from blocked pitot probes
B26.definition: Pitot probes blocked by ice, insects or covers give wrong airspeed indications, leading to warnings and autopilot disconnection.

B27.name: Crew crossed a hold-short line without clearance
B27.definition: The flight crew taxis past a runway hold-short line without a clearance to enter or cross the runway (pilot deviation).

C6.name: Clear-air turbulence with cabin injuries
C6.definition: An unexpected encounter with turbulence in clear air injures passengers or cabin crew who are standing, unbelted or near unsecured carts.

C8.name: Takeoff after de-icing holdover time exceeded
C8.definition: The aircraft is delayed after ground de-icing and the fluid holdover time is exceeded before takeoff.

C9.name: Hard landing or tail strike
C9.definition: A hard or bounced touchdown, or contact of the tail with the runway during rotation or flare.
